title: Checkpoint: Blockbusters to Pixels
objective: After this level you can reason about how business and technology together changed what films got made after 1967.
summary: Pixar grew from Lucasfilm's computer division into Toy Story's maker through a 1991 Disney deal. The chapter shows business and technology reshaping film from 1967 to 1995.

cards.headline: Chapter 9 finale: the first all-computer feature began in a director's company.
cards.body: In 1979 Lucasfilm, George Lucas's production company, hired Ed Catmull to lead its new computer division. That small team is the thread that ties this chapter's business and technology together.

cards.headline: From Lucasfilm to Pixar
cards.body: In 1986 the computer division was spun off as an independent business, Pixar, controlled by Apple cofounder Steve Jobs. In 1991 Pixar agreed with Disney to jointly develop, produce and distribute three computer-animated feature films. The first was Toy Story (1995), made by Pixar with Disney. A new technology needed a business deal before it reached a screen.

cards.headline: Money and machines, together
cards.body: Look back at the chapter. Jaws paired a nationwide opening with TV trailers. The VCR went from lawsuit to a significant share of a film's revenue. Cheap 16-mm film and pooled money let independents work outside the studios. Models, paint, puppets and cels made impossible images, until computers built them from polygons and light.

questions.prompt: A filmmaker in 1950 wants a monster to walk through a model city. Which pair of methods from this chapter fits?

options.label: Ray tracing the monster and Phong shading the city
options.rationale: Those are computer methods from later.

options.label: Stop-motion posing for the monster, and filming the city models at high speed
Cel painting the city and improvising the monster
options.rationale: Improvising is for actors, not puppets.

options.label: Time-shifting the monster onto videotape

questions.explanation: Stop motion moves the model a pose per frame; miniatures filmed faster than 24 fps look larger in playback.

questions.prompt: New Hollywood's directors rose in a studio system already weakened. What Level 48 ruling had cut the studios off from their theaters?

options.label: The Betamax decision
The Production Code
options.rationale: The Code was self-censorship, not a ruling on theaters.

options.label: Burstyn v. Wilson
The Paramount decrees, which forced studios to sell their theater chains

questions.explanation: The 1948 Paramount decrees forced the studios to sell their theaters and severely weakened the studio system.
